```
# Northwind Group consolidation: take-home assignment (v2)

Bundle ID: NWG-D0BC

1. Read `AI_Agentic_Engineer_TakeHome_v2.pdf` first. It lists what to submit and how we evaluate.
2. The input data is in `data/`. Process it as given; do not clean it by hand.
3. Quote your bundle ID (NWG-D0BC) in your submission email.

You may email up to 3 clarifying questions before you start.
===ACQ===
# Acquisition of Northwind India Pvt Ltd

- **Completion date:** 1 July 2024
- **Interest acquired:** 80% of the equity share capital
- **Consideration:** INR 690,000,000, paid in cash on completion by Northwind Inc.
  Northwind Inc. recorded the investment in USD at the spot rate on the completion date.
- **Net assets at completion** (from the completion accounts, INR):

| Item | INR |
| --- | --- |
| Equity share capital | 250,000,000 |
| Reserves and surplus at 1 April 2024 | 410,000,000 |
| Profit for 1 April to 30 June 2024 | 18,000,000 |
| **Net assets at completion** | **678,000,000** |

- Fair values of identifiable assets and liabilities equal their book values. No fair value adjustments.
- Northwind India's financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March.
===POLICIES===
# Northwind Group - accounting policies for consolidation (FY2024)

1. **Presentation currency.** The group presents its consolidated statements in GBP.
2. **Translation of entity statements into GBP.**
   - Assets and liabilities: closing rate at 31 December 2024.
   - Income and expenses: average rate for the period in which they are included in the group.
     For the US, the FY2024 average. For India, the H2 (1 July to 31 December 2024) average.
   - Equity: historical rates. Opening group equity is given in `prior_year_group.csv`.
   - Exchange differences on translation go to the translation reserve (account 3300).
   - Where a GBP rate is not given directly, use the product of the two given rates of the same type
     (for example, GBP/INR closing = GBP/USD closing x USD/INR closing).
3. **Foreign currency items inside an entity's own books.** Monetary items in a currency other than the
   entity's functional currency are retranslated at the closing rate. Differences go to profit or loss
   (group account 7300).
4. **Business combinations.** Non-controlling interest is measured at its proportionate share of net assets.
   Goodwill is held in the subsidiary's functional currency and retranslated at the closing rate.
5. **Intercompany.** Intercompany balances, income and expenses are eliminated in full. Items in transit
   at the year end are recorded by the receiving entity at the closing rate. Any remaining exchange
   difference on eliminating intercompany income and expense goes to group account 7300.
6. **Journals.** Manual journals are posted only if they are valid for FY2024. Invalid journals are not posted.
7. **Rounding.** Translate at full precision and round each reported figure to 2 decimal places.
```

---
title: How to upgrade to version 16
nav_title: Version 16
description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16.
---

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

## Use a coding agent (recommended)

Run the latest upgrade CLI from your app's directory:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
```

The CLI prepares the Next.js 16 migration guides and codemod command for the agent, then asks it to apply the changes and verify the app. See [Upgrade with a coding agent](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/agent-upgrade) for details.

## Or upgrade manually

Upgrading manually follows a few steps, in order:

1. [Set up AI agent docs](#set-up-ai-agent-docs) if you use a coding agent now or want future agent work grounded in version-matched docs.
2. [Run the upgrade codemod](#using-the-codemod).
3. If you prefer not to run the codemod, [install packages manually](#install-packages-manually).
4. Continue through the breaking changes below, run the relevant checks, and fix any remaining issues.

## Set up AI agent docs

Before upgrading, point `AGENTS.md` at version-matched Next.js docs so a coding agent can help with the remaining steps:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md
```

After upgrading, check that `AGENTS.md` points at the docs bundled with the installed version in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`. On Next.js 16.2 and later, `next dev` keeps this block up to date when it detects a coding agent. If the setup downloaded docs into `.next-docs/`, remove that directory once nothing references it. See [Version-matched documentation](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#version-matched-documentation) for the managed block and setup details.

## Using the codemod

To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160):

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
```

```bash package="npm"
npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
```

```bash package="bun"
bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest
```

The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to:

- Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration
- Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI
- Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy`
- Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs
- Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts

The `upgrade` codemod does not run every migration codemod. If your app still uses synchronous `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `draftMode()` access from the Next.js 15 compatibility period, also run the async Request APIs codemod:

```bash filename="Terminal"
npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api .
```

## Install packages manually

If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions:

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

```bash package="npm"
npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

```bash package="bun"
bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest
```

If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions.

## Node.js runtime and browser support

| Requirement   | Change / Details                                                   |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported |
| TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0`                                        |
| Browsers      | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+                 |

## Turbopack by default

Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build`

Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`.

```json filename="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "next dev --turbopack",
    "build": "next build --turbopack",
    "start": "next start"
  }
}
```

This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts:

```json filename="package.json"
```

---
title: output
description: Next.js automatically traces which files are needed by each page to allow for easy deployment of your application. Learn how it works here.
---

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

During a build, Next.js will automatically trace each page and its dependencies to determine all of the files that are needed for deploying a production version of your application.

This feature helps reduce the size of deployments drastically. Previously, when deploying with Docker you would need to have all files from your package's `dependencies` installed to run `next start`. Starting with Next.js 12, you can leverage Output File Tracing in the `.next/` directory to only include the necessary files.

Furthermore, this removes the need for the deprecated `serverless` target which can cause various issues and also creates unnecessary duplication.

## How it Works

During `next build`, Next.js will use [`@vercel/nft`](https://github.com/vercel/nft) to statically analyze `import`, `require`, and `fs` usage to determine all files that a page might load.

Next.js' production server is also traced for its needed files and output at `.next/next-server.js.nft.json` which can be leveraged in production.

To leverage the `.nft.json` files emitted to the `.next` output directory, you can read the list of files in each trace that are relative to the `.nft.json` file and then copy them to your deployment location.

### Turbopack NFT extensions

Turbopack `.nft.json` files include `fileHashes` and `symlinks` extensions:

- `fileHashes` is a parallel array with the same length and ordering as `files`. For example, `fileHashes[0]` is the hash for `files[0]`. A consumer can use the hash as a content identifier for caching or deduplicating traced assets.
- `symlinks` maps indexes in the sibling `files` array to their immediate targets. When `symlinks` is present, files without a corresponding entry can be assumed to be normal files or directories.

Traces that use [`experimental.turbopackAdditionalRoots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#additional-roots-experimental) also include the `additionalRoots` extension:

- `additionalRoots` is an ordered list of named source roots. Each root has its own `files`, `fileHashes`, and `symlinks` lists. Its `path` is relative to the directory containing the `.nft.json` file and identifies the source location on the build machine. `additionalRoots` names match those provided in `next.config.js` and are guaranteed to be valid directory names on most operating systems and filesystems.

## Automatically Copying Traced Files

Next.js can automatically create a `standalone` folder that copies only the necessary files for a production deployment including select files in `node_modules`.

To leverage this automatic copying you can enable it in your `next.config.js`:

```js filename="next.config.js"
module.exports = {
  output: 'standalone',
}
```

This will create a folder at `.next/standalone` which can then be deployed on its own without installing `node_modules`.

On Windows, creating directory symlinks [can require elevated privileges or Developer Mode](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsdeveloper/2016/12/02/symlinks-windows-10/). If standalone generation must fall back to a junction point, Windows stores an absolute target and that particular output is not relocatable.

Additionally, a minimal `server.js` file is also output which can be used instead of `next start`. This minimal server does not copy the `public` or `.next/static` folders by default as these should ideally be handled by a CDN instead, although these folders can be copied to the `standalone/public` and `standalone/.next/static` folders manually, after which `server.js` file will serve these automatically.

To copy these manually, you can use the `cp` command-line tool after you `next build`:

```bash filename="Terminal"
cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/
```

To start your minimal `server.js` file locally, run the following command:

```bash filename="Terminal"
node .next/standalone/server.js
```

<AppOnly>

> **Good to know**:
>
> - If your project needs to listen to a specific port or hostname, you can define `PORT` or `HOSTNAME` environment variables before running `server.js`. For example, run `PORT=8080 HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 node server.js` to start the server on `http://0.0.0.0:8080`.

</AppOnly>

<PagesOnly>

> **Good to know**:
>
> - `next.config.js` is read during `next build` and serialized into the `server.js` output file.
> - If your project needs to listen to a specific port or hostname, you can define `PORT` or `HOSTNAME` environment variables before running `server.js`. For example, run `PORT=8080 HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 node server.js` to start the server on `http://0.0.0.0:8080`.

</PagesOnly>

## Caveats

- While tracing in monorepo setups, the project directory is used for tracing by default. For `next build packages/web-app`, `packages/web-app` would be the tracing root and any files outside of that folder will not be included. To include files outside of this folder you can set `outputFileTracingRoot` in your `next.config.js`.

```js filename="packages/web-app/next.config.js"
const path = require('path')

module.exports = {
  // this includes files from the monorepo base two directories up
  outputFileTracingRoot: path.join(__dirname, '../../'),
}
```

- There are some cases in which Next.js might fail to include required files, or might incorrectly include unused files. In those cases, you can leverage `outputFileTracingExcludes` and `outputFileTracingIncludes` respectively in `next.config.js`. Each option accepts an object whose keys are **route globs** (matched with [picomatch](https://www.npmjs.com/package/picomatch#basic-globbing) against the route path, e.g. `/api/hello`) and whose values are **glob patterns resolved from the project root** that specify files to include or exclude in the trace.

> **Good to know**:
> In a monorepo, `project root` refers to the Next.js project root (the folder containing next.config.js, e.g., packages/web-app), not necessarily the monorepo root.

```js filename="next.config.js"
module.exports = {
  outputFileTracingExcludes: {
    '/api/hello': ['./un-necessary-folder/**/*'],
  },
  outputFileTracingIncludes: {
    '/api/another': ['./necessary-folder/**/*'],
    '/api/login/\\[\\[\\.\\.\\.slug\\]\\]': [
      './node_modules/aws-crt/dist/bin/**/*',
    ],
  },
}
```

Using a `src/` directory does not change how you write these options:

- **Keys** still match the route path (`'/api/hello'`, `'/products/[id]'`, etc.).
- **Values** can reference paths under `src/` since they are resolved relative to the project root.

```js filename="next.config.js"
module.exports = {
  outputFileTracingIncludes: {
    '/products/*': ['src/lib/payments/**/*'],
    '/*': ['src/config/runtime/**/*.json'],
  },
  outputFileTracingExcludes: {
    '/api/*': ['src/temp/**/*', 'public/large-logs/**/*'],
  },
}
```

You can also target all routes using a global key like `'/*'`:

```js filename="next.config.js"
module.exports = {
  outputFileTracingIncludes: {
    '/*': ['src/i18n/locales/**/*.json'],
  },
}
```

These options are applied to server traces and do not affect routes that do not produce a server trace file:

- Edge Runtime routes are not affected.
- Fully static pages are not affected.

In monorepos or when you need to include files outside the app folder, combine `outputFileTracingRoot` with includes:

```js filename="next.config.js"
const path = require('path')

module.exports = {
  // Trace from the monorepo root
  outputFileTracingRoot: path.join(__dirname, '../../'),
  outputFileTracingIncludes: {
    '/route1': ['../shared/assets/**/*'],
  },
}
```

> **Good to know**:
>
> - Prefer forward slashes (`/`) in patterns for cross-platform compatibility.
> - Keep patterns as narrow as possible to avoid oversized traces (avoid `**/*` at the repo root).

Common include patterns for native/runtime assets:

```js filename="next.config.js"
module.exports = {
  outputFileTracingIncludes: {
    '/*': ['node_modules/sharp/**/*', 'node_modules/aws-crt/dist/bin/**/*'],
  },
}
```

## Caching APIs

### revalidateTag

[`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error.

```ts
// Before
revalidateTag('posts')

// After
revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
```

If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead.

```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
'use server'

import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'

export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) {
  // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates
  revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max')
}
```

```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher
'use server'

import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'

export async function updateArticle(articleId) {
  // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates
  revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max')
}
```

Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background.

### updateTag

[`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.

It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request.

```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
'use server'

## ESLint Flat Config

`@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support.

Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin.

If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details.

## Scroll Behavior Override

In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `<html>` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows:

1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto`
2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top)
3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value

This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation.
```

## Removals

These features were previously deprecated and are now removed:

### AMP Support

AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed:

- `amp` configuration from your Next config file
- `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`)

```tsx
// Removed
import { useAmp } from 'next/amp'

// Removed
export const config = { amp: true }
```

- `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages

```js filename="next.config.js"
const nextConfig = {
  // Removed
  amp: {
    canonicalBase: 'https://example.com',
  },
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards.

### `next lint` Command

The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting.

A codemod is available to automate migration:

```bash package="pnpm"
pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
```

```bash package="npm"
npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
```

```bash package="yarn"
yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
```

```bash package="bun"
bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .
```

The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed.

```js filename="next.config.mjs"
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  // No longer supported
  // eslint: {},
}

export default nextConfig
```

{
  "content": "# LedgerFlow\n\n**LedgerFlow** is an AI-powered financial consolidation and reporting platform\nfor companies that operate through multiple legal entities across different\ncountries.\n\n> **Status: Phase 1 — project setup and Docker infrastructure only.**\n> The accounting engine, AI agents, file ingestion, reporting and database\n> integration are planned for later phases and are **not implemented yet**.\n\n---\n\n## The problem it solves\n\nConsider a group with a parent company in the United States (USD), a\nsubsidiary in the United Kingdom (GBP) and another subsidiary in India (INR).\nEach entity keeps its own financial records, chart of accounts and reporting\nstructure. Combining them into accurate group-level financial statements is\nhard because of:\n\n- Different currencies and exchange rates\n- Different charts of accounts\n- Intercompany transactions that must be eliminated\n- Ownership percentages and non-controlling interests (NCI)\n- Acquisition dates and business combination accounting\n- Accounting adjustments and reporting policies\n- The need to trace every reported figure back to its source\n\nLedgerFlow automates this process while maintaining complete financial\ntraceability.\n\n## Planned core capabilities\n\nThese are the intended product capabilities. **None of them are implemented\nin Phase 1** beyond the placeholder routes that will host them:\n\n1. **Source data management** — read and organize financial input files from\n   different entities.\n2. **Financial consolidation** — convert entity-level records into\n   consolidated group accounts.\n3. **AI-assisted analysis** — agents interpret accounting policies, suggest\n   account mappings, investigate anomalies and explain issues.\n4. **Deterministic accounting engine** — all financial calculations are\n   performed by Python logic, never by LLM-generated arithmetic.\n5. **Issue management** — flag missing FX rates, unbalanced journals,\n   duplicate adjustments and other inconsistencies.\n6. **Financial reporting** — consolidated trial balance, balance sheet,\n   profit and loss, and changes in equity.\n7. **Auditability** — trace every reported figure to source records,\n   adjustments, FX conversions and elimination entries.\n8. **Agent activity** — show what the AI workflow did, which tools it invoked\n   and what it recommended.\n\n## Technology stack\n\n| Layer     | Technology |\n|-----------|------------|\n| Frontend  | Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Lucide React |\n| Backend   | Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Pydantic, Uvicorn |\n| Database  | PostgreSQL (official Docker image) — infrastructure only, currently unused |\n| Storage   | Filesystem (`data/`, `storage/`, `output/`) |\n| Future AI | LangChain, LangGraph, MCP, Gemini API, Pandas, Python `Decimal` (later phases) |\n| Infra     | Docker, Docker Compose |\n\n## High-level architecture\n\n```\nBrowser ──▶ frontend (Next.js :3000) ──HTTP──▶ backend (FastAPI :8000)\n                                                     │\n                       ┌─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────┐\n                       ▼                             ▼                  ▼\n                data/ (read-only)             storage/ (rw)       output/ (rw)\n                immutable inputs              runs · issues       generated\n                                               agent logs          reports\n\ndb (PostgreSQL :5432) ── intentionally NOT connected to the application\n```\n\n- The **frontend** container runs the Next.js app and talks to the backend\n  over HTTP.\n- The **backend** container runs FastAPI and uses **filesystem-based\n  storage** for Phase 1.\n- The **db** container runs official PostgreSQL with a persistent volume,\n  present for future use. The backend has **no database connection string and\n  no dependency on the database** — the application works with the database\n  stopped.\n\nSee [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for details.\n\n## Repository structure\n\n```text\nledgerflow/\n├── frontend/           Next.js app (src/app, components, lib, hooks, types)\n├── backend/            FastAPI app (app/api, core, schemas, services,\n│                       accounting, agents, mcp, storage) + tests\n├── data/\n│   └── northwind/      Immutable original source inputs\n├── storage/            Future run/issue/agent-log state (filesystem)\n├── output/             Generated financial reports\n├── docs/               architecture.md\n├── transcripts/        Working transcripts\n├── DECISIONS.md        Key engineering decisions\n├── VALIDATION.md       Phase 1 validation results\n├── REFLECTION.md       Phase 1 reflection\n├── .env.example        Environment template (no secrets)\n├── .gitignore\n├── .dockerignore\n└── docker-compose.yml  frontend + backend + db\n```\n\n## Local development (without Docker)\n\n### Backend\n\n```bash\ncd backend\npython3.11 -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate\npip install -e \".[dev]\"\nuvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000\n```\n\n### Frontend\n\n```bash\ncd frontend\nnpm install\nnpm run dev\n```\n\n- Frontend: http://localhost:3000 (redirects to `/dashboard`)\n- Backend: http://localhost:8000\n\n### Tests and lint\n\n```bash\ncd backend && pytest            # backend tests\ncd frontend && npm run lint     # eslint\ncd frontend && npm run build    # production build\n```\n\n## Docker setup\n\n```bash\ncp .env.example .env    # optional; defaults work out of the box\ndocker compose up --build\n```\n\n| Service   | Port  | Notes |\n|-----------|-------|-------|\n| frontend  | 3000  | Next.js dashboard |\n| backend   | 8000  | FastAPI API |\n| db        | 5432  | PostgreSQL (unused by the app) |\n\nStop only the database — the application keeps working:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose stop db\n```\n\nOther useful commands:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose ps            # service status + health\ndocker compose logs -f       # follow logs\ndocker compose down          # stop and remove containers (volume persists)\ndocker compose down -v       # also remove the PostgreSQL volume\n```\n\n## API health endpoint\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:8000/api/health\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"ok\",\n  \"service\": \"ledgerflow-backend\"\n}\n```\n\n`GET /` returns basic application identification, and interactive API docs are\navailable at http://localhost:8000/docs.\n\n## Environment variables\n\nCopy `.env.example` to `.env` and adjust values. Real secrets (such as\n`GEMINI_API_KEY`) must never be committed — `.env` is git-ignored.\n\n```env\nAPP_ENV=development\nBACKEND_PORT=8000\nFRONTEND_PORT=3000\n\nPOSTGRES_DB=ledgerflow\nPOSTGRES_USER=ledgerflow\nPOSTGRES_PASSWORD=<REDACTED> Phase 1 scope\n\nImplemented: monorepo scaffold, dashboard shell with placeholder routes,\nFastAPI health/identification endpoints, Docker Compose infrastructure,\nfilesystem storage layout, documentation.\n\n**Not implemented (later phases):** accounting calculations, consolidation\nengine, FX translation, journal validation, intercompany eliminations, NCI,\nAI agents, MCP tools, Gemini integration, file ingestion, database\nintegration, authentication and full dashboard functionality.\n",

{
  "content": "# LedgerFlow — Architecture\n\n> **Phase 1.** This document describes the foundation that exists today and\n> the components planned for later phases. Nothing under \"Planned\" is\n> implemented yet.\n\n## 1. Goals\n\nLedgerFlow consolidates the financial records of a multi-entity,\nmulti-currency group into accurate group-level statements. Two principles\nshape the architecture:\n\n1. **Deterministic accounting.** All financial calculations are performed by\n   plain Python logic (later phases: `Decimal` for precision, Pandas for\n   tabular work). LLMs never do arithmetic — AI agents interpret, suggest,\n   investigate and explain, and always cite what they based a conclusion on.\n2. **Traceability.** Every reported figure must be traceable back to source\n   records, account mappings, FX conversions, adjustments and elimination\n   entries. Storage is designed around that audit trail from day one.\n\n## 2. Frontend / backend separation\n\n| | Frontend | Backend |\n|---|---|---|\n| Framework | Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript | Python 3.11+ + FastAPI |\n| Port | 3000 | 8000 |\n| Runs | Dashboard UI, routing, presentation | APIs, accounting, AI workflows, file processing |\n| Talks to backend | HTTP (`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`) | — |\n\n- The frontend never contains accounting logic; it renders what the API\n  returns.\n- The backend is framework-modular: `app/api` (HTTP layer),\n  `app/core` (configuration), `app/schemas` (Pydantic models),\n  `app/services`, `app/accounting`, `app/agents`, `app/mcp`,\n  `app/storage`.\n- CORS on the backend allows the frontend origin.\n\nPhase 1 endpoints:\n\n- `GET /` — application identification\n- `GET /api/health` — health check\n\n## 3. Docker service architecture\n\n`docker-compose.yml` defines three independent services on a dedicated\n`ledgerflow` bridge network:\n\n```text\n        browser\n           │\n           ▼\n┌─────────────────────┐    HTTP     ┌─────────────────────┐\n│ frontend            │ ──────────▶ │ backend             │\n│ Next.js · :3000     │             │ FastAPI · :8000     │\n│ healthcheck: fetch  │             │ healthcheck: urllib │\n└─────────────────────┘             └──────────┬──────────┘\n                                               │ bind mounts\n                     ┌─────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐\n                     ▼                         ▼                      ▼\n              data/  (read-only)        storage/ (rw)           output/ (rw)\n\n┌─────────────────────┐\n│ db                  │\n│ postgres:16-alpine  │   ← NOT connected to frontend or backend\n│ :5432 · pg_isready  │      no depends_on, no connection string\n│ volume: postgres_data│\n└─────────────────────┘\n```\n\nConfiguration details:\n\n- Ports come from `.env` (`FRONTEND_PORT`, `BACKEND_PORT`) with defaults.\n- `data/` is mounted **read-only** into the backend; `storage/` and `output/`\n  are mounted read-write.\n- All three services have health checks (Next `fetch`, Python `urllib`,\n  `pg_isready`).\n- The frontend receives `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` as a **build argument** (Next.js\n  inlines public env vars at build time).\n\n### PostgreSQL is present but intentionally unused\n\nPostgreSQL ships with the stack because later phases may want durable\nrelational storage. During Phase 1:\n\n- The backend has **no database connection string** anywhere in code or\n  configuration.\n- There is **no `depends_on: db`** for any service — the backend does not\n  wait for database health.\n- There are **no database models, migrations, tables or seed data**.\n- Stopping the database (`docker compose stop db`) does not affect the\n  frontend or backend.\n\n## 4. Filesystem-based persistence\n\nPhase 1 persists everything on the filesystem:\n\n```text\ndata/\n  northwind/       # Original source files — immutable, mounted read-only\n\nstorage/\n  runs/            # Future consolidation run metadata\n  issues/          # Future issue and review state\n  agent_logs/      # Future agent execution logs\n\noutput/            # Generated financial reports\n```\n\n- The backend centralises path resolution in\n  `backend/app/storage/filesystem.py` (`FileStoragePaths`), which reads\n  `DATA_DIR`, `STORAGE_DIR` and `OUTPUT_DIR` from the environment and creates\n  the writable layout on startup.\n- The accounting engine and API layers will depend on this storage boundary,\n  **not** on the underlying medium. When PostgreSQL is introduced later, it\n  slots in behind the same interface without rewriting accounting logic.\n- `data/` is treated as immutable input: the application never writes to it.\n\n## 5. Planned components (not implemented)\n\nThese belong to later phases and do not exist in the codebase yet:\n\n**Accounting (deterministic)** — trial balance ingestion, chart-of-accounts\nmapping, FX translation (closing/average/historical rates), intercompany\neliminations, business combination accounting, NCI, goodwill, accounting\nadjustments, journal validation, consolidation runs and financial statement\ngeneration.\n\n**AI layer** — LangChain and LangGraph agent workflows, MCP tool integrations,\nGemini API as the initial model provider. Agents will read accounting\npolicies, propose account mappings, investigate anomalies and explain issues.\nEvery tool call is logged to `storage/agent_logs/` for the Agent Activity UI.\n\n**Data layer** — PostgreSQL-backed persistence for runs, issues and agent logs\nreplacing or complementing the filesystem, with models and migrations.\n\n**Product** — file ingestion/upload workflows, authentication, and full\ndashboard functionality behind the placeholder routes.\n\n## 6. Repository layout\n\n```text\nfrontend/   Next.js application (src/app routes, components, lib, hooks, types)\nbackend/    FastAPI application (app/* packages, tests, pyproject.toml)\ndata/       Immutable source inputs (northwind bundle)\nstorage/    Runtime state: runs, issues, agent_logs\noutput/     Generated reports\ndocs/       Architecture documentation\n```\n\n## 7. Design decisions\n\nSee [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md) for the decision log covering this phase.\n",

{
  "content": "# Decisions\n\nEngineering decisions made while establishing LedgerFlow's foundation.\nScope: **Phase 1 only** (project setup and Docker infrastructure).\n\n---\n\n## D1. Monorepo with three top-level service directories\n\n**Decision:** Single repository containing `frontend/`, `backend/` and\ninfrastructure files at the root.\n\n**Why:** Phase 1 ships one Docker Compose stack; a monorepo keeps the\ncompose file, docs and shared `.env` next to both services. Clear\nsubdirectory boundaries keep each service independently runnable.\n\n## D2. Source data copied into `data/northwind/` byte-for-byte\n\n**Decision:** The original Northwind assignment bundle (README, PDF and all\n15 data files) was copied into `data/northwind/` with original names,\ntimestamps and content. SHA-256 checksums of the copies match the originals.\nThe original bundle in `~/Downloads` was left untouched.\n\n**Why:** The product must treat source inputs as immutable evidence for\nauditability. The backend mounts `data/` **read-only** in Docker to enforce\nthis at the infrastructure level.\n\n## D3. Filesystem persistence with a single storage boundary\n\n**Decision:** Phase 1 persists to `storage/` and `output/` via\n`backend/app/storage/filesystem.py` (`FileStoragePaths`), configured through\n`DATA_DIR` / `STORAGE_DIR` / `OUTPUT_DIR` environment variables.\n\n**Why:** Requirements forbid database integration now, but runs, issues and\nagent logs need somewhere to live in later phases. Centralising path\nresolution means PostgreSQL can later replace/augment this layer without\ntouching the accounting engine.\n\n## D4. PostgreSQL included but disconnected\n\n**Decision:** `db` (postgres:16-alpine) runs with a named volume, published\nport and health check — but the backend has **no connection string, no driver\ndependency and no `depends_on`** on it.\n\n**Why:** The brief requires the database as future infrastructure while the\napplication must work with the database stopped. Keeping it fully decoupled\nnow avoids accidental coupling (`docker compose stop db` must change nothing).\n\n## D5. Backend health check uses Python stdlib, not curl\n\n**Decision:** The backend container health check runs\n`python -c \"urllib.request.urlopen(...)\"`.\n\n**Why:** `python:3.11-slim` ships no HTTP client binary; adding `curl` would\nbloat the image. The frontend (Node) and db (`pg_isready`) use tools already\npresent in their images.\n\n## D6. # Phase 1 Complete ✅

LedgerFlow's foundation is built, validated, committed (`f83b508`), and running.

## What was created

**Source data** — The Northwind bundle was found at `~/Downloads/Northwind_TakeHome_v2` (the working directory was empty). All 17 files (README, PDF, 15 data files) copied into `data/northwind/` with original names/timestamps, **SHA-256 verified byte-identical** to the originals, and mounted into the backend **read-only**.

**Backend** (Python 3.11, FastAPI)
- `GET /` → app identification · `GET /api/health` → `{"status":"ok","service":"ledgerflow-backend"}`
- CORS for the frontend, modular packages (`api/`, `core/`, `schemas/`, `storage/` + reserved `services/`, `accounting/`, `agents/`, `mcp/`)
- `FileStoragePaths` centralizes filesystem layout (`data/`, `storage/{runs,issues,agent_logs}/`, `output/`) so PostgreSQL can later slot in behind the same seam
- Multi-stage Dockerfile (python:3.11-slim, stdlib-based healthcheck)

**Frontend** (Next.js 16, App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui base-nova, Lucide)
- Dark navy sidebar (branding, grouped nav, active states), header (page title, **live API status chip** polling `/api/health`, mobile Sheet nav), main content area
- All 7 routes: `/dashboard` (+ entities, source-data, runs, issues, reports, agent-activity) — placeholder panels that honestly state "Not implemented yet", **no invented metrics**; `/` → 307 → `/dashboard`
- Standalone multi-stage Dockerfile (node:22-alpine, non-root)

**Infrastructure & docs** — `docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `.dockerignore` (+ per-service), `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `VALIDATION.md`, `REFLECTION.md`, storage/.gitkeep layout.

## Docker services & ports

|---|---|---|
| frontend | localhost:3000 | ✅ healthy (node fetch) |
| backend | localhost:8000 | ✅ healthy (python urllib) |

directory. `backend/.dockerignore` was tightened to `**/__pycache__`-style

are fully supported on Python 3.11+ and keep behavior identical without the
marker files.

## 👤 User

# Phase 2 — LedgerFlow Agentic Backend Architecture

Implement the agentic backend architecture for LedgerFlow.

Phase 1 is complete. Before making changes, inspect the existing project structure, backend implementation, dependencies, and source data.

Work strictly inside the currently opened project directory. Do not inspect or modify files outside it. Never modify the original files under `data/northwind/`.

## 1. Architecture

Build one shared Core LangGraph Agent that powers two experiences:

- **Consolidate Agent:** Executes the end-to-end financial consolidation workflow when explicitly triggered.
- **AI Copilot:** Answers questions about source data, accounting policies, financial statements, consolidation runs, and detected issues.

Both must use the same Core Agent, Skill Registry, MCP integration, backend services, and persistence layer.

Architecture:

```text
Consolidate Agent ──┐
                    ├── Core LangGraph Agent
AI Copilot ─────────┘          |
                         Skill Registry
                               |
                   +-----------+-----------+
                   |                       |
              Consolidation          Financial Analysis
                 Skill                   Skill
                   |                       |
                   +-----------+-----------+
                               |
                          MCP Tools
                               |
                       Backend Services
                               |
                    Deterministic Accounting
```

## 2. Core LangGraph Agent

Implement a reusable LangGraph agent with:

- Typed execution state.
- Intent identification.
- Skill selection and loading.
- Tool invocation.
- Conditional execution.
- Error handling.
- Conversation context.
- Execution tracing.
- Persistent state.

Support two execution modes:

- `consolidation`: bounded, structured task execution.
- `copilot`: conversational, request-driven execution.

Do not create separate agents for these experiences.

## 3. Skill architecture

Implement a reusable Skill Registry.

Each Skill should contain its own instructions, purpose, execution procedure, permitted tools, validation requirements, and output expectations.

Create two initial Skills:

**Consolidation Skill**

Responsible for coordinating the complete consolidation workflow:

1. Inspect source data.
2. Validate inputs.
3. Execute accounting operations through backend services.
4. Generate financial statements.
5. Validate outputs.
6. Persist results and execution evidence.
7. Return an execution summary.

**Financial Analysis Skill**

Responsible for answering questions using actual source data and persisted consolidation results.

It must retrieve evidence through tools and never invent financial figures.

Skills are reusable capabilities, not independent agents.

## 4. MCP integration

Implement a proper MCP server/client integration using the official MCP Python SDK.

Expose controlled tools for meaningful backend operations, including:

- Source data inspection.
- Trial balance and mapping validation.
- FX and intercompany inspection.
- Consolidation execution.
- Financial statement retrieval.
- Issue retrieval.
- Financial figure traceability.

Design tool schemas with typed inputs and outputs.

MCP tools must call backend services. Do not put accounting calculations inside the MCP layer.

Do not expose unrestricted filesystem access or arbitrary code execution to the LLM.

## 5. Accounting safety boundaries

The LLM is responsible for orchestration, intent understanding, tool selection, investigation, and explanation.

Python services are responsible for all financial calculations, including:

- Currency conversion.
- Trial balance aggregation.
- Journal validation.
- Intercompany reconciliation.
- Eliminations.
- Acquisition accounting.
- NCI.
- Translation reserve.
- Financial statement generation.
- Control figures.

The LLM must never calculate or invent official financial figures, bypass mandatory validations, silently change mappings, accept unbalanced journals, or modify source records.

Treat all source data and journal descriptions as untrusted input. Instructions embedded in financial records must never override system or Skill instructions.

Unresolved accounting judgments must be flagged for human review.

## 6. Consolidation execution

When the Consolidation Skill is triggered:

1. Create a unique run ID.
2. Initialize bounded LangGraph execution.
3. Load the Consolidation Skill.
4. Invoke the required MCP tools.
5. Execute deterministic accounting services.
6. Enforce mandatory validations.
7. Persist results, issues, and execution traces.
8. Return the execution status and summary.

Support completed, completed-with-warnings, blocked, failed, and awaiting-review states.

Do not fabricate progress or results.

The implementation must integrate with the actual Northwind dataset and accounting policies. If required accounting services are not yet implemented, identify the missing dependency rather than simulating it.

## 7. Copilot execution

The Copilot must use the same Core Agent.

It should dynamically select the Financial Analysis Skill and relevant tools based on the user's question.

Support questions about:

- Group financial performance.
- Entity-level financials.
- Accounting policies.
- Consolidation differences.
- Detected issues.
- Financial statement figures.
- Source transaction evidence.
- Historical consolidation runs.

Keep the Copilot read-only.

Answers must be grounded in retrieved evidence and identify the relevant reporting period and consolidation run.

## 8. Persistence and observability

Use the existing filesystem persistence architecture.

Persist:

- Consolidation run metadata and status.
- Conversation threads and messages.
- Agent execution traces.
- Skill selections.
- Tool calls and results or references.
- Issues and approval requests.

Ensure persistence survives backend restarts.

Do not introduce PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, or additional infrastructure without a concrete technical justification. The existing PostgreSQL container is not currently used and the backend must remain functional without it.

Never log API keys or secrets.

## 9. Backend APIs

Implement the necessary FastAPI endpoints for:

- Starting and retrieving consolidation runs.
- Checking execution status.
- Retrieving outputs and issues.
- Sending Copilot messages.
- Retrieving conversation threads.
- Retrieving agent execution traces.

Use Pydantic schemas, proper error handling, and asynchronous execution where appropriate.

Follow existing backend conventions.

## 10. Tests

Add tests covering:

- Core Agent execution.
- Skill discovery and selection.
- MCP tool invocation and validation.
- Consolidation workflow enforcement.
- Copilot evidence retrieval.
- Tool failures.
- Human-review conditions.
- Persistence and thread isolation.
- Read-only Copilot behavior.

Use mocked LLM responses for deterministic tests and actual Northwind data for integration tests where the required accounting services exist.

## 11. Implementation process

Work in these milestones:

**Milestone 1:** Inspect the repository and present the architecture, dependency assessment, and implementation plan. Do not modify code. Wait for approval.

**Milestone 2:** Implement Core LangGraph Agent, typed state, Skill Registry, and persistence. Add tests.

**Milestone 3:** Implement MCP integration and controlled tools. Add tests.

**Milestone 4:** Implement Consolidation and Financial Analysis Skills. Integrate actual backend services and add tests.

**Milestone 5:** Implement backend APIs, execution tracing, and end-to-end verification.

Stop after each milestone and report files changed, implementation decisions, tests executed, and remaining issues. Wait for approval before continuing.

## Constraints

- Do not rebuild the frontend in this phase.
- Do not create separate agents for individual Skills.
- Do not duplicate accounting logic.
- Do not use LLMs for official financial calculations.
- Do not fabricate missing accounting services or outputs.
- Do not modify original source data.
- Do not introduce unnecessary infrastructure.
- Preserve existing working Phase 1 functionality.

Start with Milestone 1 only.

months = sorted({r['month'] for r in ipl})\nprint('in_pl_monthly: ledgers', led)\nprint('in_pl_monthly: months', months[0], '..', months[-1], f'({len(months)})')\n\""

## 2. Source data inspection (computed, read-only)

All three TBs balance (US Dr=Cr=43,534,373.43 · UK Σ=0 · IN Dr=Cr=1,805,000,000). The dataset contains **real seeded defects** the platform must detect — these are test fixtures, not data to fix:

| Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Unbalanced journal | `JE-006` out by **+1,200.00** |
| Out-of-period journal | `JE-017` dated **2025-01-06** (policy §6: only FY2024 journals post) |
| Duplicate-looking accrual | `JE-014` vs `JE-019` (both US FY2024 audit fee) |
| Unmapped journal account | `JE-016` uses `IN-GST-ITC` — absent from `map_in.csv` |
| Subledger control mismatch | UK AR & AP each off by **45,000** (US/IN tie exactly) |
| Unmatched intercompany doc | `INV-US-2291` recorded by US, **no UK counterpart** (in transit) |
| Suspicious mapping | `map_uk`: 2310 Deferred income → **4100 Revenue** (CoA has 2300) |
| Missing FX rate | GBP/SGD has only opening+average — **no closing** for UK's SGD monetary item; GBP/INR must be derived per policy (product of rates) |
| Structural quirks | UK signed-balance format + duplicate code 7000 (cost centres) + 3-char codes (0030/0031); IN `dr_cr` format; US already group-coded; IN monthly P&L = 8 ledgers × 9 months |

## 4. Architecture (matches your diagram)

```text
POST /api/runs ──► Consolidate Agent ──┐
POST /api/copilot/messages ──► AI Copilot ──┤
                                          ▼
                     ┌── Core LangGraph Agent (ONE StateGraph) ──┐
                     │  load_context → identify_intent → select_skill
                     │  → [skill procedure] → finalize (persist)  │
                     │  typed AgentState · trace events · errors  │
                     └────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                                Skill Registry
                     (mode allowlist: consolidation | copilot, read-only flags)
                    ┌─────────────────┴──────────────────┐
           Consolidation Skill                Financial Analysis Skill
           (bounded fixed pipeline)           (dynamic tool selection)
                    └─────────────────┬──────────────────┘
                          Tool Gateway (policy: skill-permitted tools only,
                          read-only enforcement, max calls, arg validation)
                                      │
                              MCP client ──HTTP──► MCP server (FastMCP, /mcp)
                                      │                    │
                                      │             Backend Services
                                      │  source_data · validation · run ·
                                      │  issue · statement-retrieval · thread
                                      ▼
                          Filesystem persistence (storage/*)
```

**Two execution modes, one graph:**
- **`consolidation`** — deterministic, bounded: intent comes from the request (no LLM needed to execute); the skill runs a fixed 7-step pipeline through the Tool Gateway; LLM is used only for the optional narrative summary (rule-based fallback when unconfigured). Mandatory validation gates are **graph nodes, not LLM choices** — the gateway denies any attempt to skip them.
- **`copilot`** — conversational: intent identification via LLM (structured output) with deterministic fallback; dynamically selects the Financial Analysis Skill and a read-only tool subset; conversation context loaded from persisted threads.

**Safety boundaries (§5)** realized structurally: LLM outputs only tool *calls*; every call → gateway → MCP → Python service. Calculations exist only in services. Prompt-injection defense: tool results are rendered as untrusted data blocks in messages; system+skill instructions carry higher precedence markers; source strings are never parsed as instructions.

## 5. Accounting services — the critical boundary (approval needed)

| Service category | Examples | Status | Phase 2 handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source parsing/inspection | TB/mapping/FX/IC/journal readers | **build** | Real readers over `data/northwind` (read-only) |
| Validation/control services | TB balance, subledger controls, mapping coverage, journal balance/period/duplicate, IC pairing, FX completeness | **build** | §4 explicitly mandates these MCP tools; all hit the real defects in §2 |
| Run/issue/thread/trace services | lifecycle + persistence | **build** | |
| **Calculation services** | FX translation, TB aggregation/posting, eliminations, acquisition/NCI/goodwill, translation reserve, statement generation, control figures | **missing** | **Identified as named dependencies** — never simulated. Runs terminate **`blocked`** with stage-level detail: `stages 1–2 pass (real results), stage 3 partial (journals validated, posting engine missing), stage 4–5 blocked: missing [fx_translation, consolidation_engine, statement_generator]` |

All detected defects are persisted as real **issues** (some `awaiting_review`, e.g., the suspicious 2310 mapping = accounting judgment for human review). Copilot answers grounded in **source evidence + run/issue history**, and states plainly when a consolidated figure doesn't exist yet.

## 6. MCP tools (all → services, typed Pydantic schemas)

`inspect_source_data` · `read_trial_balance` · `validate_trial_balance` · `validate_account_mappings` · `inspect_fx_rates` · `inspect_intercompany` · `validate_adjustments` · `execute_consolidation` · `get_consolidation_run` · `get_financial_statement` (typed not-available) · `list_issues` · `trace_figure` (source-level lineage works; consolidated lineage → typed unavailable). **No filesystem/code-execution tools.**

**Transport:** FastMCP mounted at `/mcp` (streamable HTTP) on the existing FastAPI app; Core Agent uses a real MCP client session (`MCP_SERVER_URL`, default `http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`). Tests use `mcp.shared.memory` in-memory sessions → zero extra infrastructure, real client/server in production.

## 7. Persistence (filesystem only, restart-safe)

```
storage/runs/<run_id>/run.json          # status, stages, summary, missing deps
storage/issues/<issue_id>.json           # incl. approvals (awaiting_review)
storage/agent_logs/threads/<thread_id>.json   # conversation messages
storage/agent_logs/traces/<trace_id>.jsonl    # intent, skill, every tool call/result
```
Atomic writes (tmp+rename); LangGraph `MemorySaver` for in-flight checkpoints with the filesystem store as source of truth; startup reconciliation converts orphaned `running` → `failed(interrupted)`. No Postgres/Redis/Celery. Secrets never logged (redaction at the trace layer).

## 8. API surface (§9)

GET  /api/runs · /api/runs/{id}   list/status/summary/stages

GET  /api/runs/{id}/issues · GET /api/issues[/{id}]
POST /api/copilot/messages        {thread_id?, text} → answer + citations + period/run refs
GET  /api/copilot/threads · /api/copilot/threads/{id}
GET  /api/agent/traces[?run_id|thread_id] · /api/agent/traces/{id}
GET  /mcp                          MCP streamable HTTP
```
Pydantic schemas, typed error model, async execution, follows existing `api/` + `schemas/` conventions.

{
  "content": "\"\"\"Filesystem storage helpers.\n\nPhase 1 persists everything on the filesystem. This module centralises\npath resolution so later phases (runs, issues, agent logs, reports) share\none storage boundary — and so PostgreSQL can be introduced later behind\nthe same interface without touching the accounting engine.\n\nPhase 2 adds the persistence primitives used by the agentic layer:\natomic JSON writes, JSONL append (traces) and safe reads. All writes go\nthrough :func:`atomic_write_json` so a crash never leaves a half-written\nfile, and persisted state survives backend restarts.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Iterator\n\nfrom app.core.config import settings\nfrom app.core.errors import StorageError\n\n\nclass FileStoragePaths:\n    \"\"\"Resolve and expose the LedgerFlow filesystem layout.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        data_dir: str | Path | None = None,\n        storage_dir: str | Path | None = None,\n        output_dir: str | Path | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        self.data_dir = Path(data_dir or settings.data_dir)\n        self.storage_dir = Path(storage_dir or settings.storage_dir)\n        self.output_dir = Path(output_dir or settings.output_dir)\n\n    @property\n    def runs_dir(self) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Future consolidation run metadata.\"\"\"\n        return self.storage_dir / \"runs\"\n\n    @property\n    def issues_dir(self) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Future issue and review state.\"\"\"\n        return self.storage_dir / \"issues\"\n\n    @property\n    def agent_logs_dir(self) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Future agent execution logs.\"\"\"\n        return self.storage_dir / \"agent_logs\"\n\n    @property\n    def threads_dir(self) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Persisted conversation threads (copilot).\"\"\"\n        return self.agent_logs_dir / \"threads\"\n\n    @property\n    def traces_dir(self) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Agent execution traces (JSONL).\"\"\"\n        return self.agent_logs_dir / \"traces\"\n\n    @property\n    def source_data_dir(self) -> Path:\n        \"\"\"Immutable source inputs (e.g. data/northwind).\"\"\"\n        return self.data_dir\n\n    def ensure_layout(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Create writable directories if they do not exist.\n\n        The source data directory is never created or modified here; it is\n        treated as immutable input.\n        \"\"\"\n        for directory in (\n            self.storage_dir,\n            self.runs_dir,\n            self.issues_dir,\n            self.agent_logs_dir,\n            self.threads_dir,\n            self.traces_dir,\n            self.output_dir,\n        ):\n            directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n\nstorage_paths = FileStoragePaths()\n\n\n# --- persistence primitives -------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef atomic_write_json(path: str | Path, data: Any) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write JSON atomically (temp file in the same dir + ``os.replace``).\"\"\"\n    target = Path(path)\n    try:\n        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(\n            prefix=f\".{target.name}.\", suffix=\".tmp\", dir=str(target.parent)\n        )\n        try:\n            with os.fdopen(fd, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n                json.dump(data, handle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, default=str)\n                handle.flush()\n                os.fsync(handle.fileno())\n            os.replace(tmp_name, target)\n        finally:\n            if os.path.exists(tmp_name):\n                os.unlink(tmp_name)\n    except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive\n        raise StorageError(f\"failed to write {target}\", details={\"path\": str(target)}) from exc\n\n\ndef read_json(path: str | Path) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Read a JSON file. Raises ``StorageError`` when it does not exist.\"\"\"\n    target = Path(path)\n    if not target.is_file():\n        raise StorageError(f\"missing json file: {target}\", details={\"path\": str(target)})\n    try:\n        with target.open(\"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            return json.load(handle)\n    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:\n        raise StorageError(\n            f\"unreadable json file: {target}\", details={\"path\": str(target)}\n        ) from exc\n\n\ndef append_jsonl(path: str | Path, record: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one JSON record as a line (used for execution traces).\"\"\"\n    target = Path(path)\n    try:\n        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        with target.open(\"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            handle.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + \"\\n\")\n    except OSError as exc:\n        raise StorageError(\n            f\"failed to append to {target}\", details={\"path\": str(target)}\n        ) from exc\n\n\ndef iter_jsonl(path: str | Path) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Yield records from a JSONL file, skipping malformed lines.\"\"\"\n    target = Path(path)\n    if not target.is_file():\n        raise StorageError(f\"missing jsonl file: {target}\", details={\"path\": str(target)})\n    with target.open(\"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        for line in handle:\n            line = line.strip()\n            if not line:\n                continue\n            try:\n                yield json.loads(line)\n            except json.JSONDecodeError:\n                continue\n",

  "content": "\"\"\"Execution tracing for the core agent.\n\nEach execution gets one JSONL trace file (``storage/agent_logs/traces/<trace_id>.jsonl``).\nEvents are appended as they happen so a run can be reconstructed after the\nfact. All payloads pass through :func:`redact` before they are written, so\nsecrets (API keys, tokens) can never leak into a stored trace.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable\n\nfrom app.storage.filesystem import append_jsonl, iter_jsonl\n\n# Keys whose values are always masked, regardless of content.\n_SENSITIVE_KEY_RE = re.compile(\n    r\"(api[_-]?key|authorization|bearer|password|secret|token|credential)\",\n    re.IGNORECASE,\n)\n\n# Values that look like common API key formats.\n_SENSITIVE_VALUE_RES = [\n    re.compile(r\"AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\\-]{35}\"),  # Google API key\n    re.compile(r\"sk-[0-9A-Za-z_\\-]{16,}\"),  # generic secret key\n]\n\n_MASK = \"***REDACTED***\"\n\n\ndef redact(value: Any, extra_secrets: Iterable[str] = ()) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Recursively mask secrets in strings, dicts and lists.\"\"\"\n    secrets = [s for s in extra_secrets if s and len(s) >= 8]\n\n    if isinstance(value, str):\n        out = value\n        for secret in secrets:\n            if secret in out:\n                out = out.replace(secret, _MASK)\n        for pattern in _SENSITIVE_VALUE_RES:\n            out = pattern.sub(_MASK, out)\n        return out\n    if isinstance(value, dict):\n        redacted: dict[Any, Any] = {}\n        for key, item in value.items():\n            if isinstance(key, str) and _SENSITIVE_KEY_RE.search(key):\n                redacted[key] = _MASK\n            else:\n                redacted[key] = redact(item, secrets)\n        return redacted\n    if isinstance(value, list):\n        return [redact(item, secrets) for item in value]\n    if isinstance(value, tuple):\n        return tuple(redact(item, secrets) for item in value)\n    return value\n\n\ndef _now() -> str:\n    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n\n\nclass TraceRecorder:\n    \"\"\"Append-only JSONL recorder bound to a single execution trace.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, traces_dir: str | Path, trace_id: str) -> None:\n        self.trace_id = trace_id\n        self.path = Path(traces_dir) / f\"{trace_id}.jsonl\"\n        self._seq = 0\n\n    def event(\n        self,\n        event: str,\n        payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,\n        *,\n        secrets: Iterable[str] = (),\n    ) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Append one event; returns the record that was written.\"\"\"\n        self._seq += 1\n        record = {\n            \"ts\": _now(),\n            \"seq\": self._seq,\n            \"trace_id\": self.trace_id,\n            \"event\": event,\n            \"payload\": redact(payload or {}, secrets),\n        }\n        append_jsonl(self.path, record)\n        return record\n\n    def read_events(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"Read back every event recorded for this trace.\"\"\"\n        if not self.path.is_file():\n            return []\n        return list(iter_jsonl(self.path))\n",

{
  "content": "\"\"\"Conversation thread persistence.\n\nThreads (copilot conversations) are stored as one JSON file per thread under\n``storage/agent_logs/threads/<thread_id>.json``. Messages are serialised to\nplain dicts so they survive a backend restart with no database.\n\nThe thread id is the only isolation key: two threads never share a file, so\nseparate conversations cannot bleed into one another.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable\n\nfrom langchain_core.messages import (\n    AIMessage,\n    AnyMessage,\n    HumanMessage,\n    SystemMessage,\n    ToolMessage,\n)\n\nfrom app.core.errors import NotFoundError, StorageError\nfrom app.storage.filesystem import atomic_write_json, read_json\n\n_MESSAGE_TYPES: dict[str, type] = {\n    \"human\": HumanMessage,\n    \"ai\": AIMessage,\n    \"system\": SystemMessage,\n    \"tool\": ToolMessage,\n}\n\n\ndef serialize_message(message: AnyMessage) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Convert a LangChain message into a JSON-safe dict.\"\"\"\n    record: dict[str, Any] = {\"type\": message.type, \"content\": message.content}\n    if message.additional_kwargs:\n        record[\"additional_kwargs\"] = message.additional_kwargs\n    if isinstance(message, ToolMessage):\n        record[\"name\"] = message.name\n        record[\"tool_call_id\"] = message.tool_call_id\n    return record\n\n\ndef deserialize_message(record: dict[str, Any]) -> AnyMessage:\n    \"\"\"Rebuild a LangChain message from its stored dict.\"\"\"\n    msg_type = record.get(\"type\", \"human\")\n    cls = _MESSAGE_TYPES.get(msg_type, HumanMessage)\n    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {\"content\": record.get(\"content\", \"\")}\n    if record.get(\"additional_kwargs\"):\n        kwargs[\"additional_kwargs\"] = record[\"additional_kwargs\"]\n    if cls is ToolMessage:\n        kwargs[\"name\"] = record.get(\"name\", \"\")\n        kwargs[\"tool_call_id\"] = record.get(\"tool_call_id\", \"\")\n    return cls(**kwargs)\n\n\nclass ThreadService:\n    \"\"\"Read/write conversation threads on the filesystem.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, threads_dir: str | Path) -> None:\n        self.threads_dir = Path(threads_dir)\n\n    def _path(self, thread_id: str) -> Path:\n        if not thread_id or \"/\" in thread_id or \"\\\\\" in thread_id or \"..\" in thread_id:\n            raise StorageError(\n                \"invalid thread id\", details={\"thread_id\": thread_id}\n            )\n        return self.threads_dir / f\"{thread_id}.json\"\n\n    def exists(self, thread_id: str) -> bool:\n        return self._path(thread_id).is_file()\n\n    def load(self, thread_id: str) -> list[AnyMessage]:\n        \"\"\"Return the stored messages for a thread ([] when it does not exist).\"\"\"\n        path = self._path(thread_id)\n        if not path.is_file():\n            return []\n        data = read_json(path)\n        if not isinstance(data, dict):\n            raise StorageError(\n                \"corrupt thread record\", details={\"thread_id\": thread_id}\n            )\n        return [deserialize_message(m) for m in data.get(\"messages\", [])]\n\n    def meta(self, thread_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Thread metadata (mode, timestamps) without the messages.\"\"\"\n        path = self._path(thread_id)\n        if not path.is_file():\n            raise NotFoundError(\n                \"thread not found\", details={\"thread_id\": thread_id}\n            )\n        data = read_json(path)\n        return {k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != \"messages\"}\n\n    def save(\n        self,\n        thread_id: str,\n        messages: Iterable[AnyMessage],\n        *,\n        mode: str | None = None,\n        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,\n    ) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"Atomically persist a thread's messages (created_at is preserved).\"\"\"\n        path = self._path(thread_id)\n        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n        created_at = now\n        if path.is_file():\n            try:\n                existing = read_json(path)\n                created_at = existing.get(\"created_at\", now)\n            except StorageError:\n                pass\n\n        record: dict[str, Any] = {\n            \"thread_id\": thread_id,\n            \"mode\": mode,\n            \"created_at\": created_at,\n            \"updated_at\": now,\n            \"messages\": [serialize_message(m) for m in messages],\n        }\n        if metadata:\n            record[\"metadata\"] = metadata\n        atomic_write_json(path, record)\n        return record\n\n    def list(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n        \"\"\"List every persisted thread (metadata only).\"\"\"\n        if not self.threads_dir.is_dir():\n            return []\n        out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n        for path in sorted(self.threads_dir.glob(\"*.json\")):\n            data = read_json(path)\n            if isinstance(data, dict):\n                out.append({k: v for k, v in data.items() if k != \"messages\"})\n        return out\n\n    def delete(self, thread_id: str) -> None:\n        path = self._path(thread_id)\n        if not path.is_file():\n            raise NotFoundError(\n                \"thread not found\", details={\"thread_id\": thread_id}\n            )\n        path.unlink()\n",

Each skill declares which\nexecution modes may use it.\n\nThe LLM orchestrates; the skill's ``execute`` does the work by calling typed\nbackend services (never by doing financial arithmetic in the prompt).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom abc import ABC, abstractmethod\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Any, TYPE_CHECKING\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\n\nfrom app.agents.state import AgentMode, SkillResult, ToolCallRecord\n\nif TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover\n    from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel\n\n    from app.agents.tracing import TraceRecorder\n\n\nclass ToolPolicy(str, Enum):\n    \"\"\"What a skill is allowed to do through the MCP tool gateway.\"\"\"\n\n    READ_ONLY = \"read_only\"\n    ALLOWED_TOOLS = \"allowed_tools\"   # subset of tools, enforced by name\n    NO_TOOLS = \"no_tools\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass SkillSpec:\n    \"\"\"Static metadata describing a skill.\n\n    This is what the agent (and a human reviewer) can inspect to understand\n    a skill before it runs.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    purpose: str\n    instructions: str\n    execution_procedure: tuple[str, ...]\n    permitted_tools: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    validation_requirements: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    output_expectations: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    allowed_modes: frozenset[AgentMode] = frozenset()\n    tool_policy: ToolPolicy = ToolPolicy.NO_TOOLS\n    description: str = \"\"\n\n    def validate(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Reject an incomplete skill definition early.\"\"\"\n        missing = [\n            f\n            for f in (\"name\", \"purpose\", \"instructions\")\n            if not getattr(self, f).strip()\n        ]\n        if not self.execution_procedure:\n            missing.append(\"execution_procedure\")\n        if not self.allowed_modes:\n            missing.append(\"allowed_modes\")\n        if missing:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"skill '{self.name or '<unnamed>'}' is missing: {', '.join(missing)}\"\n            )\n\n\nclass SkillContext(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Everything a skill receives when it executes.\n\n    Deliberately explicit: the skill gets the structured intent, the raw\n    user input, the LLM handle (for composing answers only), the trace\n    recorder, and a tool gateway (MCP) when one is configured. The skill\n    must call backend services for all calculations.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    mode: AgentMode\n    intent: Any\n    user_input: str | None = None\n    payload: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)\n    llm: Any = None\n    trace: Any = None\n    tool_gateway: Any = None\n    settings: Any = None\n\n    model_config = {\"arbitrary_types_allowed\": True}\n\n\nclass Skill(ABC):\n    \"\"\"Base class for every skill registered with the core agent.\"\"\"\n\n    spec: SkillSpec\n\n    @property\n    def name(self) -> str:\n        return self.spec.name\n\n    @abstractmethod\n    async def execute(self, context: SkillContext) -> SkillResult:\n        \"\"\"Run this skill and return its typed result.\"\"\"\n\n    def permitted_tool_names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        return self.spec.permitted_tools\n\n    def allows_mode(self, mode: AgentMode) -> bool:\n        return mode in self.spec.allowed_modes\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ExecutionReport:\n    \"\"\"Convenience accumulator a skill can build while executing.\"\"\"\n\n    tool_calls: list[ToolCallRecord] = field(default_factory=list)\n    issues: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)\n    data: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)\n",

{
  "content": "\"\"\"Skill Registry: the single source of truth for agent capabilities.\n\nExactly one registry instance is shared by the Consolidation Agent and the\nAI Copilot. Skills declare which modes they serve; the registry enforces\nthat declaration so a copilot request can never reach a consolidation-only\nskill (and vice versa).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Iterable\n\nfrom app.agents.skills.base import Skill, SkillSpec\nfrom app.agents.state import AgentMode\nfrom app.core.errors import (\n    SkillNotAllowedForModeError,\n    SkillNotFoundError,\n)\n\n\nclass SkillRegistry:\n    \"\"\"Register, look up and validate skills for the core agent.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, skills: Iterable[Skill] | None = None) -> None:\n        self._skills: dict[str, Skill] = {}\n        for skill in skills or ():\n            self.register(skill)\n\n    # -- registration -------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def register(self, skill: Skill) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a skill. Raises on duplicates or incomplete metadata.\"\"\"\n        spec = skill.spec\n        spec.validate()\n        if spec.name in self._skills:\n            raise ValueError(f\"skill already registered: {spec.name}\")\n        self._skills[spec.name] = skill\n\n    def register_spec(\n        self, skill: Skill, spec: SkillSpec\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Attach a spec to a skill then register it.\"\"\"\n        skill.spec = spec\n        self.register(skill)\n\n    def replace(self, skill: Skill) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Register or overwrite (used to swap in mocks during tests).\"\"\"\n        skill.spec.validate()\n        self._skills[skill.spec.name] = skill\n\n    def unregister(self, name: str) -> None:\n        self._skills.pop(name, None)\n\n    # -- lookup -------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    def get(self, name: str) -> Skill:\n        \"\"\"Return a skill by name.\n\n        Raises:\n            SkillNotFoundError: When no skill has that name.\n        \"\"\"\n        skill = self._skills.get(name)\n        if skill is None:\n            raise SkillNotFoundError(\n                f\"skill not found: {name}\", details={\"skill\": name}\n            )\n        return skill\n\n    def has(self, name: str) -> bool:\n        return name in self._skills\n\n    def names(self) -> list[str]:\n        return sorted(self._skills)\n\n    def all(self) -> list[Skill]:\n        return [self._skills[n] for n in self.names()]\n\n    def for_mode(self, mode: AgentMode) -> list[Skill]:\n        \"\"\"Skills permitted to run in ``mode``, sorted by name.\"\"\"\n        return [s for s in self.all() if s.allows_mode(mode)]\n\n    def resolve(\n        self, name: str, mode: AgentMode, *, allow_unregistered: bool = False\n    ) -> Skill:\n        \"\"\"Look up ``name`` and assert it is allowed to run in ``mode``.\n\n        Raises:\n            SkillNotFoundError: When the skill is not registered and\n                ``allow_unregistered`` is False.\n            SkillNotAllowedForModeError: When the skill exists but does not\n                serve this execution mode.\n        \"\"\"\n        if name not in self._skills:\n            if allow_unregistered:\n                raise SkillNotFoundError(\n                    f\"skill not found: {name}\",\n                    details={\"skill\": name, \"mode\": mode.value},\n                )\n            raise SkillNotFoundError(\n                f\"skill not found: {name}\", details={\"skill\": name}\n            )\n        skill = self._skills[name]\n        if not skill.allows_mode(mode):\n            allowed = sorted(m.value for m in skill.spec.allowed_modes)\n            raise SkillNotAllowedForModeError(\n                f\"skill '{name}' is not allowed in mode '{mode.value}'\",\n                details={\"skill\": name, \"mode\": mode.value, \"allowed_modes\": allowed},\n            )\n        return skill\n\n    def select_by_intent(\n        self, intent_kind: str, mode: AgentMode, *, hint: str | None = None\n    ) -> Skill | None:\n        \"\"\"Pick the skill for an intent.\n\n        A ``hint`` (the LLM's proposed skill) wins when it is valid for the\n        mode; otherwise we fall back to the first mode-allowed skill whose\n        name matches the intent kind. Returns ``None`` when nothing matches\n        (the caller decides whether that is fatal).\n        \"\"\"\n        if hint and self.has(hint):\n            try:\n                return self.resolve(hint, mode)\n            except SkillNotAllowedForModeError:\n                raise\n        candidates = self.for_mode(mode)\n        if not candidates:\n            return None\n        for skill in candidates:\n            if skill.spec.name == intent_kind:\n                return skill\n        return candidates[0] if len(candidates) == 1 else None\n\n    def describe(self, mode: AgentMode | None = None) -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"Return skill metadata (for API responses and agent prompts).\"\"\"\n        skills = self.all() if mode is None else self.for_mode(mode)\n        return [\n            {\n                \"name\": s.spec.name,\n                \"description\": s.spec.description,\n                \"purpose\": s.spec.purpose,\n                \"allowed_modes\": sorted(m.value for m in s.spec.allowed_modes),\n                \"permitted_tools\": list(s.spec.permitted_tools),\n                \"execution_procedure\": list(s.spec.execution_procedure),\n                \"validation_requirements\": list(s.spec.validation_requirements),\n                \"output_expectations\": list(s.spec.output_expectations),\n            }\n            for s in skills\n        ]\n\n\ndef build_default_registry() -> SkillRegistry:\n    \"\"\"Registry with the core skills.\n\n    Phase 2 Milestone 4 wires in the Consolidation and Financial Analysis\n    skills; until then this returns an empty registry so the agent can be\n    exercised with registered test skills.\n    \"\"\"\n    return SkillRegistry()\n",

-- helpers ------------------------------------------------------------\n\n    @property\n    def _recursion_limit(self) -> int:\n        return max(10, self.runtime.settings.agent_max_graph_steps)\n\n    def _history(self, thread_id: str | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n        if not thread_id:\n            return []\n        messages = self.runtime.thread_service.load(thread_id)\n        from app.agents.thread_service import serialize_message\n\n        return [serialize_message(m) for m in messages]\n\n    def _persist_thread(\n        self, thread_id: str | None, mode: AgentMode, messages: Iterable[Any]\n    ) -> None:\n        if not thread_id:\n            return\n        self.runtime.thread_service.save(thread_id, messages, mode=mode.value)\n\n    # Persist the conversation only when the turn produced messages\n        # (failed turns leave the thread untouched).\n        final_messages = final_state.get(\"messages\") or []\n        if effective_thread and final_messages:\n            self._persist_thread(effective_thread, mode, final_messages)\n\n        return self._to_result(run_id, trace_id, mode, effective_thread, final_state)\n\n    def _load_messages(self, thread_id: str | None) -> list[Any]:\n        if not thread_id:\n            return []\n        return self.runtime.thread_service.load(thread_id)\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _to_result(\n        run_id: str,\n        trace_id: str,\n        mode: AgentMode,\n        thread_id: str | None,\n        state: AgentState,\n    ) -> ExecutionResult:\n        return ExecutionResult(\n            run_id=run_id,\n            trace_id=trace_id,\n            thread_id=thread_id,\n            mode=mode,\n            status=state.get(\"status\", RunStatus.FAILED),\n            summary=state.get(\"summary\"),\n            intent=state.get(\"intent\"),\n            skill_name=state.get(\"skill_name\"),\n            skill_result=state.get(\"skill_result\"),\n            tool_calls=list(state.get(\"tool_calls\") or []),\n            errors=list(state.get(\"errors\") or []),\n            warnings=list(state.get(\"warnings\") or []),\n        )\n",

| File | Role |
|---|---|
